title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 152
paragraphs: Now, whether Xerxes actually sent a herald to Argos saying these things, and whether the Argive envoys who went up to Susa really questioned Artaxerxes about friendship, I cannot say for certain; and I offer no opinion on the matter other than what the Argives themselves report. But I do know this: if all the nations of men were to bring together in one place the evils they have suffered, wishing to make an exchange with their neighbors, each people, once they had closely examined the evils their fellows had suffered, would gladly carry back home those they had brought. So the Argives have not acted the most shamefully of all. I, however, am bound to report what is reported, though I am not bound to believe it entirely; and let this remark be taken as holding good for every narrative in my history. For I must add that it is also reported that the Argives were actually the ones who invited the Persian to invade Greece, because their war with the Lacedaemonians had ended badly, and they were ready to suffer anything rather than the calamity that was then upon them.
